subject: How to run RStan unit tests?

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: How to run RStan unit tests?
parts:
I want to add some more tests to verify that refactoring doesnt completely tank RStan.

How can I fire off the unit tests in RStan? It looks like there's been some activity lately, so hopefully someone can guide me.

messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] How to run RStan unit tests?
parts:
First, run 'make build' to make sure it can be built.

Second, run 'make check'

Third, there is an r script at folder call test.

All the above can be seen from the script on Jenkins

--
Jiqiang

I want to add some more tests to verify that refactoring doesnt completely tank RStan.

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] How to run RStan unit tests?
parts:
Thanks! Just in case anyone wants to follow along, you can type this from the rstan directory:

git submodule init
git submodule update
cd stan
git fetch
git checkout origin/develop
cd ..
git submodule status
cd rstan
make clean
make install_pre_rpkg
make check && (cd tests & R -q -f runRunitTests.R --args ../rstan.Rcheck)

I can't actually run make check on my machine. I'm having a problem building the vignette. Hopefully this is a quick fix. So far, I've figured out that the error message reported by R CMD build actually hides the true error message in the vignette.

When I type:
> R CMD Sweave rstan/vignettes/rstan_vignette.Rnw

I get this error:
...
Warning in file(fname, "rt") :
  cannot open file 'schools.stan': No such file or directory
Error in file(fname, "rt") : cannot open the connection

When I run from the rstan/vignettes directory on rstan_vignette.Rnw, it works fine.

Is there an easy way to specify the working directory and possibly hide that output?


Daniel
